clinicalSummary: Brought in with profuse rice-water diarrhoea and vomiting for 2 days after attending a funeral gathering in Budiriro. Severe dehydration, BP 80/50 on arrival. Started on aggressive IV rehydration but arrested 3 hours after admission despite resuscitation. Stool sample sent for cholera confirmation.

Market vendor with sudden-onset profuse watery diarrhoea, muscle cramps and prostration. Brought in with profound dehydration and weak pulse; died despite IV fluids and antibiotics. Post-mortem rapid test positive for Vibrio cholerae.

Referred in extremis after a prolonged home delivery attended by an untrained attendant. Arrived in hypovolaemic shock from postpartum haemorrhage with a retained placenta. Transfused 4 units and taken to theatre but arrested intra-operatively. Baby survived. Referred to MPDSR committee.

Presented unconscious with a 4-day history of fever and rigors following recent travel to a malaria-endemic lowveld area near Chipinge. RDT positive for P. falciparum, parasitaemia high. Developed seizures and deteriorated despite IV artesunate — cerebral malaria. Pronounced dead at 06:45.

Known hypertensive and type-2 diabetic. Collapsed at home with crushing central chest pain radiating to the left arm. Cardiac arrest on arrival in casualty; resuscitated for 40 minutes without return of spontaneous circulation. ECG changes consistent with acute anterior STEMI.

Admitted 5 days ago with a left-sided hemiplegic stroke and dysphagia. Developed fever, productive cough and hypoxia on day 3 — aspiration pneumonia on chest X-ray. Failed to respond to broad-spectrum antibiotics and oxygen. Died of respiratory failure.
